defects.description: Plan hand-rolls unsigned base64 JSON cursors in the invoices route instead of reusing the signed encodeCursor/decodeCursor in src/lib/pagination.ts. The cursors carry no tenant or filter binding, so they can be forged, and R3/R5/AC2/AC3 (a cursor is only valid for its own tenant and filters) cannot be enforced. This contradicts the NFR that cursors be unforgeable and consistent with /v1/customers.

Keyset uses created_at only (created_at < $after, ORDER BY created_at DESC) with no id tie-break, so invoices sharing a timestamp are skipped at page boundaries. That violates R2 and AC1 (60 rows with one created_at).
A malformed cursor silently returns the first page, contradicting R5/AC4 (400 invalid_cursor). The plan's test even asserts the wrong behaviour.

Plan removes offset support, but R6/AC5 require offset to keep working for 90 days with Deprecation and Link headers and a 400 invalid_pagination when combined with cursor. Removing offset is explicitly out of scope.
defects.location: plan.md step 6; spec.md R6, Out of scope

defects.description: Step 1 ships a DDL migration (new index) despite the NFR change freeze that bans migrations in this release.

The performance reasoning is wrong. An index on (tenant_id, status) does not serve ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC, so for a common status like 'paid' Postgres may choose it and then sort a large share of 2M rows, missing AC6. Performance is only checked after rollout prep, by EXPLAIN on staging.
defects.location: plan.md step 1; plan.md Test strategy; fixture/migrations/003_invoices.sql

defects.description: No tests for the shared-timestamp boundary (AC1 is only tested with distinct timestamps), cross-tenant cursor reuse (AC2), filter mismatch (AC3) or offset deprecation (AC5), and the garbage-cursor test asserts the opposite of AC4.

tensions.description: Consistency wants the migration removed because of the DDL freeze. Risk sees that the planned index doesn't serve the sort and wants the migration changed to a better composite index, such as (tenant_id, status, created_at, id). One fix deletes the migration and the other rewrites it. The way out depends on noticing that migration 003 already defines (tenant_id, created_at DESC, id DESC).
tensions.lens_a_fix: Drop migrations/004 entirely; no DDL ships during the freeze.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Replace the (tenant_id, status) index with a composite index matching the filter plus sort order so AC6 holds.
tensions.reconciliation: Ship no migration. Write the keyset query as (created_at, id) < ($c, $i) with ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC so it walks the existing invoices_tenant_created_idx from 003, applying status and created_after as filters during the walk. Verify AC6 with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before rollout. Note a status-leading composite index as a post-freeze follow-up if the filtered path proves slow.

tensions.description: Architecture's natural fix is to reuse decodeCursor and copy the /v1/customers pattern. That pattern deliberately treats a null (invalid) cursor, or one from another tenant, as 'start from the first page'. Consistency requires 400 invalid_cursor for malformed, tampered or mismatched cursors. Copying the existing route's behaviour reproduces the defect consistency flags, and making the shared helper throw would change /v1/customers, which is out of scope.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Delete the hand-rolled helpers; use encodeCursor/decodeCursor from lib/pagination.ts the way routes/customers.ts does, including the tenant check.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Return 400 invalid_cursor for malformed, tampered, wrong-tenant, or wrong-filter cursors per R5/AC2-AC4.
tensions.reconciliation: Reuse encodeCursor/decodeCursor with the payload {c, i, t: tenantId, f: filter hash}. In the invoices route only, throw ValidationError('invalid_cursor') when decodeCursor returns null or t or f mismatch. Leave lib/pagination.ts and /v1/customers unchanged, since altering the shared helper would change customers' behaviour and that is out of scope.
